questions.title: Integer File Echo Drill
questions.description:
Read an integer n from stdin. Open the file /tmp/atom_day20_int.txt in write mode, write n to it, then close the file. Reopen the file in read mode, read the integer back, and print GOT <value>.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
A single line: GOT <n>.

Constraints:
-100000 <= n <= 100000

questions.title: File Modes r w a Drill
questions.description:
Read an integer n from stdin. Using the file /tmp/atom_day20_mode.txt demonstrate all three text modes: first open in "w" mode and write n, then close; reopen in "a" mode and write n+1, then close; reopen in "r" mode and read both integers, then close. Print VALUES <n> <n+1>.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
A single line: VALUES <n> <n+1>.

Constraints:
-100000 <= n <= 100000

questions.title: Read Line from File Drill
questions.description:
Read a single line of text (up to 255 characters) from stdin. Write that line to /tmp/atom_day20_line.txt in write mode, then close. Reopen the file in read mode, use fgets to read the line back into a buffer, strip the trailing newline if present, then close the file and print the line.

Input Format:
A single line of text (no leading/trailing spaces, may contain interior spaces).

Output Format:
A single line containing the text that was written.

Constraints:
Line length 1..255

questions.title: Write Numbers File Drill
questions.description:
Read an integer N followed by N integers from stdin. Write each integer on its own line to /tmp/atom_day20_nums.txt in write mode, then close. Reopen the file in read mode and count how many integers can be read back (using fscanf in a loop), then close. Print COUNT <k>.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N. Line 2: N space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single line: COUNT <k> where k is the number of integers read back.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -10000 <= each integer <= 10000

questions.title: Binary Int Archive Drill
questions.description:
Read an integer n from stdin. Open /tmp/atom_day20_binint.bin in binary write mode ("wb") and write the integer using fwrite, then close. Reopen the file in binary read mode ("rb"), use fread to read the integer back, then close. Print BIN <value>.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
A single line: BIN <n>.

Constraints:
-100000 <= n <= 100000

questions.title: File Open NULL Guard Drill
questions.description:
Read an integer n from stdin. Open /tmp/atom_day20_guard.txt in write mode; if fopen returns NULL, print FAIL and stop. Otherwise write n to the file, close, then reopen in read mode (also checking for NULL and printing FAIL on failure), read the integer back, close, and print OK <value>.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
A single line: OK <n> on success, or FAIL if any fopen returns NULL.

Constraints:
-100000 <= n <= 100000

questions.title: Inventory Quantity Ledger Writer
questions.description:
A warehouse clerk records a single quantity q (the number of units received in a shipment). Write q to /tmp/atom_day20_inv.txt as text in write mode, then close. Reopen the file in read mode, read the integer back, close, and print STORED <q> to confirm the persistence round-trip.

Input Format:
A single integer q.

Output Format:
A single line: STORED <q>.

Constraints:
0 <= q <= 100000

questions.title: Student Score Card Recorder
questions.description:
A teacher records a single student's exam score s on a card persisted at /tmp/atom_day20_score.txt. Write s to the file in write mode, close, reopen in read mode, read the score back, close, and print SCORE <s> <grade> where grade is A when s >= 80, B when 60 <= s < 80, otherwise F.

Input Format:
A single integer s.

Output Format:
A single line: SCORE <s> <grade>.

Constraints:
0 <= s <= 100

questions.title: Sensor Log Append Drill
questions.description:
An environmental sensor logs a temperature reading t (in degrees Celsius). First write t to /tmp/atom_day20_sensor.txt in write mode, then close. Then reopen the file in append mode ("a") and write t+1 (a calibration-adjusted reading), then close. Finally reopen the file in read mode, read both integers back, then close and print LOG <t> <t+1>.

Input Format:
A single integer t.

Output Format:
A single line: LOG <t> <t+1>.

Constraints:
-50 <= t <= 100

questions.title: Config File Read-back Reporter
questions.description:
A daemon writes a port-number config line of the form PORT=

to /tmp/atom_day20_cfg.txt. Read the port p from stdin, write the config line in write mode, then close. Reopen the file in read mode, read its entire content character-by-character using fgetc and echo each byte to stdout, then close. Input Format: A single integer p (the port number). Output Format: The exact file content, which is the line PORT=

followed by a newline. Constraints: 0 <= p <= 65535

questions.title: Classroom Marks File Aggregator
questions.description:
A teacher wants to compute the total of a class's marks but the school's grading tool only exposes file I/O primitives — no fscanf/fgets for reading back the marks file. Read N then N integers from stdin, write each on its own line to /tmp/atom_day20_marks.txt in write mode, then close. Reopen the file in read mode, parse the integers manually using fgetc (digit by digit, respecting a leading minus sign), compute the sum, then close and print SUM <s>.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N. Line 2: N space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single line: SUM <s>.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -10000 <= each mark <= 10000

questions.title: Warehouse Stock Append Log
questions.description:
A warehouse records N stock movements (signed integers: positive means inbound, negative means outbound). Open /tmp/atom_day20_stock.txt in write mode and write the first movement, then close. Reopen in append mode and write the remaining movements, then close. Reopen in read mode, parse all integers manually with fgetc (no fscanf/fgets/fread allowed), compute the net stock movement, then close and print NET <x>.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N. Line 2: N space-separated signed integers.

Output Format:
A single line: NET <x>.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -10000 <= each movement <= 10000

questions.title: Binary Student Record Archive
questions.description:
A school persists student records (roll number and marks) as a binary file for compact storage. Read N then N pairs (roll, marks) from stdin. Define a struct with two int members (roll and marks). Open /tmp/atom_day20_studrec.bin in binary write mode, write all N records with a single fwrite call, then close. Reopen in binary read mode, read the records back with a single fread call into a local array, then close. Print TOTAL <total_marks> COUNT <n_read>.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N. Next N lines: <roll> <marks> per line.

Output Format:
A single line: TOTAL <sum_of_marks> COUNT <n_read>.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= roll <= 99999, 0 <= marks <= 100

questions.title: Log File Character Frequency Reporter
questions.description:
A log scanner must classify characters in a one-line log message. Read the line from stdin using a getchar loop (stopping at newline or EOF, no fgets allowed). Open /tmp/atom_day20_log.txt in write mode, write the line followed by a newline using fprintf, then close. Reopen the file in read mode, scan every character with fgetc, count digit characters and alphabetic characters (manually, not via ctype.h helpers), then close and print DIGITS <d> ALPHA <a>.

Input Format:
A single line of text (may contain interior spaces).

Output Format:
A single line: DIGITS <d> ALPHA <a>.

Constraints:
Line length 1..1023

questions.title: Append-only Audit Trail Builder
questions.description:
An audit service records N event identifiers (integers) to /tmp/atom_day20_audit.txt with the prefix EVT: per line. First open the file in write mode and write a single header line containing just # (to truncate any prior content), then close. Then reopen in append mode and append EVT:<id> for each event, then close. Finally reopen in read mode, scan the file byte-by-byte with fgetc (no fscanf/fgets/fread), and count how many EVT: lines exist, then close and print EVENTS <k>.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N. Line 2: N space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single line: EVENTS <k>.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -10000 <= id <= 10000

questions.title: Temperature Series Binary File
questions.description:
A weather station stores a series of N temperature readings as a binary file of doubles for compactness. Read N then N integers (each representing a temperature in degrees Celsius) from stdin. Convert each to a double. Open /tmp/atom_day20_temps.bin in binary write mode, write the array of doubles with a single fwrite, then close. Reopen in binary read mode, read them back with a single fread, then close. Compute the average temperature and print AVG <x.xx> with two decimal places.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N. Line 2: N space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single line: AVG <avg> with exactly two decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -100 <= each temperature <= 100

questions.title: Binary Inventory Database Query
questions.description:
A store maintains an inventory database persisted as a binary file of structs. Read N then N records (id, qty, price as a double) from stdin. Define a struct with int id, int qty, double price. Open /tmp/atom_day20_invent.bin in binary write mode and write all records with one fwrite, then close. Reopen in binary read mode, read the records back with one fread, then close. Compute the total inventory value (sum of qty * price over all records) and find the id of the record whose qty*price is the largest (use a manual loop, no qsort). Print VALUE <v.xx> TOP_ID <id>.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N. Next N lines: <id> <qty> <price> per line (price is a floating-point number).

Output Format:
A single line: VALUE <v.xx> TOP_ID <id> with two decimals for the value.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= id <= 99999, 0 <= qty <= 10000, 0.00 <= price <= 10000.00

questions.title: Transaction Ledger Append and Reconcile
questions.description:
A banking ledger grows in two phases: initial postings (N transactions) followed by end-of-day adjustments (M transactions). All transactions are signed integers (positive = credit, negative = debit). Open /tmp/atom_day20_ledger.txt in write mode, write the first N transactions one per line, then close. Reopen in append mode, write the next M transactions one per line, then close. Reopen in read mode, parse every integer manually with fgetc (no fscanf/fgets/fread), summing them as the final balance. Close and print BALANCE <b>.

Input Format:
Line 1: two integers N and M. Next N+M lines each contain one signed integer (or all on subsequent lines space/newline separated).

Output Format:
A single line: BALANCE <b>.

Constraints:
1 <= N, M <= 500, N+M <= 1000, -10000 <= each transaction <= 10000

questions.title: Employee Records Binary File Index Search
questions.description:
An HR system stores N employee records (id and salary) as a binary file of structs. Read N then N records (id, salary) from stdin. Define a struct with two int members. Open /tmp/atom_day20_emp.bin in binary write mode and write the records with one fwrite, then close. Then read a query id Q from stdin. Reopen the file in binary read mode. Use fseek to position the stream at the i-th record (offset = i * sizeof(struct)) and fread one record at a time, searching for the one whose id equals Q. Close the file. If found, print SALARY <salary>; otherwise print NOT_FOUND.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N. Next N lines: <id> <salary> per line. Final line: integer Q (the query id).

Output Format:
A single line: SALARY <salary> on match, else NOT_FOUND.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= id <= 999999, 0 <= salary <= 1000000

questions.title: Multi-Mode File Error Resilience
questions.description:
A resilient file manager tests both its success path and its failure path. Read two integers n and c from stdin. When c == 0, attempt to open the (never-created) file /tmp/atom_day20_no_such_file.txt in read mode; if fopen returns NULL (as it should) print OPEN_FAILED and stop; otherwise close the file and print UNEXPECTED. When c == 1, open /tmp/atom_day20_resilient.txt in write mode (checking for NULL), write n via fprintf, close, reopen in read mode (checking for NULL), parse the integer back manually with fgetc (digit by digit, respecting a leading minus sign), close, and print FINAL <value>.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers: n and c.

Output Format:
A single line: OPEN_FAILED (when c == 0) or FINAL <n> (when c == 1).

Constraints:
-100000 <= n <= 100000, c in {0, 1}
